key_insight: Plasma APOE4 proteotyping can closely mirror DNA-based APOE ε4 genotyping for identifying carrier status and even distinguishing heterozygous from homozygous carriers.
clinical_relevance: If validated broadly, this blood-based assay could offer a scalable alternative for APOE-related risk stratification and research enrollment in Alzheimer’s disease.
method: Measured plasma APOE4 with the NULISAseq CNS panel in four cohorts.
Used ADRC to set thresholds for ε4 carrier status and copy number.
Validated performance against DNA genotyping and compared associations with amyloid positivity, CDR scores, and CDR-SB worsening.
evidence_signal: Performance was very strong: AUC 0.977 in ADRC and 1.000 in three external cohorts for ε4 carrier detection, with similar AD-related associations to genotype-based analyses.
watch_item: The findings are promising but need broader real-world validation before plasma proteotyping can replace genotyping in routine clinical use.
paper_title: Clinical utility of plasma APOE proteotyping for Alzheimer's disease risk and prognosis
